claims.text: Pulumi has a new component state migrations feature that lets component authors ship the upgrade path with the component itself.
A Pulumi component state migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion for component state migrations feedback exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
A Pulumi docs guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering component state migrations and the callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repository contains an example at aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration with v1, v2 and v3 programs and migration code.
A link to the Pulumi Components concepts page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/components/.
The legacy component is `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc`, and the first version of the example creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC would require replacing the security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per the AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId documentation).
The example does not create a database.
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The modern AWSX VPC component is `awsx.ec2.Vpc`.
The third version of the example removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

In the example, the v1 resource tree has awsx:x:ec2:Vpc as the root with child Subnet and InternetGateway components; v2 has awsx:ec2:Vpc with an aws Vpc child and subnet 'vpc-isolated-1' and the internet gateway beneath the VPC; v3 has aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc as root with subnet, route table, association and internet gateway.
Pulumi's state records both physical resources and the components that group them; each record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have a cloud provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts the managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.

Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible, but cannot by themselves remove component wrappers and transfer references to the replacing resources.
A component registers a state migration by passing a migration callback through the `stateMigrations` resource option, together with an alias for the legacy component type.
The Pulumi state migration callback receives the saved state of the aliased old component followed by the state of its children.
The state migration callback returns `newState`, the complete set of records that should replace the old component and its children.
The state migration callback returns `successors`, a map from each old URN that disappears to the URN that takes its place.

In the example's migration callback, an unexpected component type raises an error instead of guessing how to migrate it, and if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources the callback does nothing.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record and changes its URN, type, and parent while preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.

The `successors` entries let the Pulumi engine update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, so the security group's reference to the VPC stays connected to the migrated VPC record, which retains the same AWS VPC ID.
The third version of the example declares the VPC, subnet, route table, association, and internet gateway directly with `@pulumi/aws`.

The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and moves the managed VPC into its place, with both the old component and its VPC child mapping to the new VPC record; the VPC keeps its AWS ID.
In the third version, the VPC registration keeps aliases for both previous component types and both migration callbacks.
Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next callback.
A stack still using legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to the plain AWS version, and a stack already on modern AWSX skips the first migration.
Once both migrations have run, both callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a state migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for any remaining changes.
In the example, the upgrade can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags even though resource IDs are kept.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
When upgrading the example, the preview should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.

When component authors register a state migration inside the component implementation, users do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update.
For an internal component change that keeps the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during both previews and updates when prior state exists for the resource.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
A Pulumi state migration callback must return no result when the resource state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite resource state without performing provider operations (no provider calls such as create, update, or read are made).
A Pulumi component state migration callback is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN that is omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The Pulumi state migrations option reference page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/ has a 'callback-api' section that explains the callback API.
The state entries passed to Pulumi component state migration callbacks use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema (pulumi-resource-state).
The Pulumi checkpoint resource format includes fields such as `urn`, `type`, `id`, `parent`, `provider`, `inputs`, and `outputs`.
The Pulumi developer docs page at pulumi-developer-docs.readthedocs.io deployment-schema.html has a 'pulumi-resource-state' section describing the checkpoint resource format.
A Pulumi component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
In Pulumi, the restrictions on state-changing migration results (for update plans and targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied state migration.
